Context from the previous page: Gauss is computing a sequence of angle transformations, apparently of Landen/AGM type for an elliptic integral. The evidence is the quadratically shrinking constants g, g', g'' (log g ≈ 8.91, log g' ≈ 7.22, log g'' ≈ 3.84) and the formulas sin 2u = g sin T, sin T' = h sin T / cos^2 u. He then introduces auxiliary angles U by a tan U = b tan T, a' tan U' = b' tan T', and so on. Under these he obtains two relations, the second of which he marks 'Gut.':
  (A) sin T' = sin((T+U)/2) / cos((T-U)/2)
  (B) cos T' = sin U' / sqrt(tan T tan U)
This page derives consequences of (A) and (B). It shows how the quantity cos(T+U), normalized in three ways, passes over into the primed angles.

Implicit steps (mine):
1. From (A): cos^2 T' = [cos^2((T-U)/2) - sin^2((T+U)/2)] / cos^2((T-U)/2).
   Using cos^2 A - sin^2 B = cos(A+B) cos(A-B) with A = (T-U)/2, B = (T+U)/2, the numerator is cos T cos U.
   Hence cos^2 T' = cos T cos U / cos^2((T-U)/2).
2. From (B): sin^2 U' = cos^2 T' tan T tan U = sin T sin U / cos^2((T-U)/2).
3. Therefore cos(T'+U') cos(T'-U') = cos^2 T' - sin^2 U' = (cos T cos U - sin T sin U) / cos^2((T-U)/2) = cos(T+U) / cos^2((T-U)/2).

The three lines on the page:
(i) Dividing step 3 by step 1 gives
    cos(T+U)/(cos T cos U) = cos(T'+U') cos(T'-U') / cos^2 T'.
(ii) Dividing step 3 by step 2 gives
    cos(T+U)/(sin T sin U) = cos(T'+U') cos(T'-U') / sin^2 U'.
(iii) Take the geometric mean of (i) and (ii), using cos T cos U sin T sin U = (1/4) sin 2T sin 2U. Equivalently, cos T' sin U' = (1/2) sqrt(sin 2T sin 2U) / cos^2((T-U)/2). This gives
    2 cos(T+U)/sqrt(sin 2T sin 2U) = cos(T'+U') cos(T'-U') / (cos T' sin U').

Purpose: these are transformation rules carrying a symmetric expression in (T, U) to an expression in (T', U'). They are presumably meant for iterating the AGM/Landen step and tracking how such a quantity behaves along the sequence (T, U) -> (T', U') -> (T'', U'').
